cases.conditions: Both ports make the same complete declarations for this profile.
cases.title: Identical molecular SMILES contracts are exact matches
cases.why: Both ports declare the same molecular SMILES format and syntax features.

cases.conditions: The source feature set is a subset of the target feature set.
cases.title: An input may accept more syntax features than the output emits
cases.why: Every optional syntax feature the output may emit is understood by the input.

cases.conditions: One port omits the required syntax feature declaration.
cases.title: Missing syntax capability information is unknown
cases.why: The comparison cannot determine which optional SMILES features the output may emit.

cases.conditions: The output may emit stereochemistry and the input does not declare support for it.
cases.title: Unsupported stereochemistry is incompatible
cases.why: Passing the string could discard stereochemical meaning that the output may encode.

cases.conditions: The output may emit isotopes and the input does not declare support for them.
cases.title: Unsupported isotopes are incompatible
cases.why: Passing the string could discard isotope information that the output may encode.

cases.conditions: The output may emit disconnected components and the input does not declare support for them.
cases.title: Unsupported disconnected components are incompatible
cases.why: The input cannot safely consume salts or other dot-disconnected components the output may emit.

cases.conditions: The required molecular SMILES declarations match and only excluded canonicalisation metadata differs.
cases.title: Canonicalisation labels do not gate this profile
cases.why: This connection consumes molecular SMILES and does not require a particular canonical form.

cases.conditions: Both ports make the same complete declarations for this profile.
cases.title: Identical protein-sequence contracts are exact matches
cases.why: The same complete sequence declaration can connect without conversion or approval.

cases.conditions: Both ports declare different alphabets and no translation step is supplied.
cases.title: Different sequence alphabets are incompatible
cases.why: Amino-acid and nucleotide strings do not have the same biological interpretation.

cases.conditions: The source omits the encoding required by the target contract.
cases.title: Missing sequence encoding is unknown
cases.why: The sequence cannot be interpreted reliably when its encoding is not declared.

cases.conditions: Both ports declare different coordinate systems and no conversion is supplied.
cases.title: Different coordinate systems are incompatible
cases.why: Coordinates in different systems cannot be consumed as if their numerical values have the same spatial meaning.

cases.conditions: The source omits the structure origin required by the target contract.
cases.title: Missing structure origin is unknown
cases.why: Experimental, predicted and otherwise derived structures have different provenance and limitations.

cases.conditions: Both ports make the same complete declarations for this profile.
cases.title: Identical protein-structure contracts are exact matches
cases.why: The same complete structure declaration can connect without conversion or approval.
